facts.raw_span: A 13-year-old boy with T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia
receiving maintenance therapy (daily 6-mercaptopurine, weekly methotrexate, monthly vincristine and dexamethasone)
3 months of hematochezia
two to three loose bowel movements per day (Bristol type 5–6) with mixed blood
polyethylene glycol produced looser stools without reducing bleeding
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, rashes, arthritis, oral or perianal lesions
intermittently neutropenic and consistently lymphopenic
abdomen was soft and nontender
a small nonbleeding external hemorrhoid was noted
Stool studies, including culture and PCR for Clostridioides difficile, cytomegalovirus, and adenovirus, were negative
Colonoscopy showed multiple semisessile, nonbleeding 1–5 mm polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa
histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains
A 13-year-old boy with T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia
receiving maintenance therapy (daily 6-mercaptopurine, weekly methotrexate, monthly vincristine and dexamethasone)
3 months of hematochezia
two to three loose bowel movements per day (Bristol type 5–6) with mixed blood
polyethylene glycol produced looser stools without reducing bleeding
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, rashes, arthritis, oral or perianal lesions
intermittently neutropenic and consistently lymphopenic
abdomen was soft and nontender
a small nonbleeding external hemorrhoid was noted
Stool studies, including culture and PCR for Clostridioides difficile, cytomegalovirus, and adenovirus, were negative
Colonoscopy showed multiple semisessile, nonbleeding 1–5 mm polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa
histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains

concepts.why: The presence of basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions in histiocytes, which are strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid-Schiff stains, is characteristic of Whipple disease.

The patient's history of T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia and immunosuppressive therapy, combined with the presence of erythematous, eroded mucosa and mixed inflammatory infiltrate, suggests a possible diagnosis of graft-versus-host disease.

Although stool studies for cytomegalovirus were negative, the patient's immunocompromised state and the presence of hematochezia and mixed inflammatory infiltrate make CMV colitis a possible diagnosis.
The patient's intermittent neutropenia and the presence of erythematous, eroded mucosa and mixed inflammatory infiltrate suggest a possible diagnosis of neutropenic colitis.

The patient's symptoms of hematochezia, loose bowel movements, and mixed inflammatory infiltrate are consistent with inflammatory bowel disease, although the diagnosis would require further evaluation.

The presence of basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions in histiocytes that are strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains, in a patient with a history of immunosuppression due to T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia and negative stool studies, points towards Malakoplakia.

rationales.F01: T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia is not specific to any of the listed conditions
rationales.F02: Maintenance therapy may contribute to neutropenia, which is a risk factor for neutropenic colitis
rationales.F03: Hematochezia is a nonspecific symptom that can be seen in various conditions
rationales.F07: Neutropenia is a risk factor for neutropenic colitis and other infections
rationales.F10: Negative stool studies help rule out Clostridioides difficile and cytomegalovirus infections
rationales.F12: The presence of basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions in histiocytes is characteristic of Malakoplakia
